name: chess-openings

description.en: 37 well-known chess openings and the moves that define them. Front: the opening's name, e.g. "Ruy Lopez (Spanish Opening)" or "Sicilian Defence"; back: its defining moves in standard algebraic notation with English piece letters (K, Q, R, B, N), e.g. "1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5", with the ECO code in a note. Every move sequence was replayed with python-chess. Moves and codes from the lichess-org/chess-openings data set and Wikidata, checked against the Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings codes as listed by Wikipedia and against 365Chess.
description.sv: 37 välkända schacköppningar och de drag som definierar dem. Framsida: öppningens namn, t.ex. ”Spanskt parti” eller ”Sicilianskt parti”; baksida: de definierande dragen i algebraisk notation med engelska pjäsbokstäver (K, Q, R, B, N i stället för svenska K, D, T, L, S), t.ex. ”1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5”, med ECO-koden i en anteckning. Varje dragföljd har spelats upp med python-chess. Drag och koder kommer från datamängden lichess-org/chess-openings och Wikidata och är kontrollerade mot koderna i Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings så som Wikipedia återger dem och mot 365Chess.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (python-chess, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

1. Candidates (Wikidata): query 1 listed every item with an ECO code (P9838), 320 rows, ordered by the number of Wikipedia language editions with an article on it, with English and Swedish labels. Queries 2 and 3 added the items' English and Swedish Wikipedia sitelinks and Swedish aliases (and found the King's Gambit, Q194506, which has no P9838). Query 4 fetched, for the 37 chosen items, every English, Swedish and multilingual label and alias and every P9838 value: each item has an English (or multilingual) alias that is its defining move sequence, written with a space after each move number ("1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5").

2. Moves and ECO codes (lichess-org/chess-openings): the five TSV files (eco, name, pgn) were downloaded from the master branch (query 6; head commit 5a13018, 2026-10-03). The README says that each opening name has a unique shortest line; for every card, the back is that shortest line under the exact lichess name (e.g. "Ruy Lopez", "Italian Game: Giuoco Piano", "Sicilian Defense: Najdorf Variation") and the note's ECO code is that row's code. The lines were rewritten without the space after the move number ("1.e4" instead of "1. e4"); castling is written with the letter O as in the data set. The selection, the English front names and the notes are the compiler's own.

3. Selection: the compiler chose the main openings and defences after 1.e4, 1.d4 and 1.c4 that are commonly taught and played at master level, the main gambits, and five of the most famous named variations (Berlin, Marshall, Najdorf, Dragon, Winawer). An opening was taken only if lichess, the Wikidata alias, the English Wikipedia article and the Swedish Wikipedia agree on its defining moves. Openings that sources define differently, or as a set-up reachable by several move orders, were left out; see Selection.

4. ECO codes: compare.py (query 12) parsed the English Wikipedia "List of ECO codes" (revision 1376141224), which gives the head line of every code with a page reference to the first edition of the Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings (Matanović, 1974–1979) and to the 2010 edition (Veličković). A line belongs to the code whose head line is its longest prefix. With all head lines, this rule gives every card the same code as lichess. editions.py (query 12) applied the rule to each edition separately: 35 cards have the same code in both; the Four Knights Game is C47 in 2010 but C46 in the first edition (whose C47 begins with 4.d4), and the Grünfeld Defence is D80 in 2010 while the first edition's D80 begins only with 4.Bg5. For the Grünfeld the rule gives no first-edition code of its own: the first edition's D70 head is "1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 with d7–d5", which is not a move prefix (so the rule falls back to E61, a King's Indian code), and its D71–D79 begin 3.g3 d5; no source states which first-edition code covers 3.Nc3 d5, so the deck does not name one. The two cards give the 2010 (and lichess) code and say so in the note; the Four Knights note names the first-edition C46, which 365Chess also gives, and the Grünfeld note says only where the first edition's D80 begins. Wikidata's P9838 was compared too: it states the card's exact code for 8 openings, a range starting at it for 26 (the code range of the opening family), another range for the Grünfeld (D70–D99), none for the King's Gambit, and C77 for the Ruy Lopez (see quality control).

5. Moves cross-check: compare.py compared every lichess line with the infobox "moves" of the English Wikipedia article on the opening (query 7; for the King's Gambit Accepted and the Winawer Variation the article on the parent opening, whose text names the line), with the Swedish Wikipedia list "Lista över schacköppningar" (revision 53530900; Swedish piece letters S, L, T, D translated to N, B, R, Q) and the Swedish articles' infobox "drag", and with the 365Chess ECO index (queries 9). No move sequence disagreed. Where a list's entry is a shorter head line that the card's line extends (for example C44 "1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6" for the Scotch Game), the evidence says so. The evidence on every card was generated from the parsed data by make_dossier.py (query 14), except the readings of the Swedish articles' text, which were written by hand from the saved wikitext.

6. Swedish names: each Swedish front is the title of the Swedish Wikipedia article on the opening, which is also the item's svwiki sitelink in Wikidata (for example "Spanskt parti", "Sicilianskt parti", "Preussiskt parti" for the Two Knights Defence, "Wienerparti", "Löparspel", "Moderna försvaret"). Wikidata's own sv labels often differ from these titles and some are wrong ("Skotsk gambit" on the Scotch Game, "Phillidors försvar"); the article titles were preferred. Where the Swedish Wikipedia treats an opening in a section of a broader article, the Swedish name is the one that section uses: "Antagen kungsgambit" and "Antagen damgambit"/"Avböjd damgambit" (Kungsgambit, Damgambit), "Nordisk gambit" for the Danish Gambit (Centrumspel), "Benkögambit" (Benoniförsvaret), and for the named variations the parent's name followed by the variation, "Spanskt parti: Berlinerförsvaret", "Spanskt parti: Marshallangreppet", "Sicilianskt parti: Najdorfvarianten", "Sicilianskt parti: Drakvarianten", "Franskt parti: Winawervarianten", matching the English fronts ("Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defence"). The Swedish Wikipedia list confirms these forms ("Spanskt, Berlinerförsvaret", "Sicilianskt, drakvarianten", "Kungsgambit, antagen"). Nationalencyklopedin (ne.se) was tried as a second Swedish reference (query 11) but its pages returned only the site's shell or an error to the research environment, and no Sveriges Schackförbund material listing opening names was found by web search; the Swedish names therefore rest on the Swedish Wikipedia and Wikidata's sitelinks alone. For the ten names above that Wikidata does not give (the Najdorf item's sv label is the longer "Najdorfvarianten i Sicilianskt parti"), the Swedish Wikipedia is their only source; see Licensing.

7. English names: English (British) spelling throughout ("Defence"), in the form most English sources use (Wikidata label or alias, lichess, the English Wikipedia article title). Variations are written "Opening: Variation" as lichess does. Alternative names that help a learner are in the notes (Russian Game, Robatsch Defence, Centre Counter Defence, Volga Gambit, Italian Game), each a Wikidata alias or lichess name (written in British spelling) and confirmed by the Wikipedia articles or 365Chess. The Swedish notes name the Swedish alternative names tvåspringarspel, Volgagambit and nordisk gambit, found in the Swedish Wikipedia, Petrovs försvar and Robatschs försvar (article redirects), and Giuoco Piano (Wikidata's mul label).

8. Machine checks: verify_moves.py (query 13, python-chess 1.11.2) read the finished dossier (run again after the review rounds) and replayed every back from the initial position: the move numbers must be in step, every move legal and written exactly as python-chess writes it in standard algebraic notation (so piece letters, capture signs, check signs and castling are canonical), the final position must equal the one recorded in the card's evidence, and the back must equal the shortest lichess line under the card's lichess name. As a test of the test, each back with its last move replaced by an impossible queen move was replayed and had to be rejected. All 37 cards passed every check and all 37 mutations were caught. The builder checks against live Wikidata, for every card, that the item has the back's move sequence as an English or multilingual alias, compared character for character with Wikidata's string (a space after each move number; 10 of the aliases it uses are written with no-break spaces, U+00A0, and the check uses them as they are), and where Wikidata states them, the exact ECO code (P9838) and the English and Swedish names (and, for the Englund Gambit, that the item is named after Fritz Englund, P138). The built deck was validated with the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators (validate_sources.ts).
selection: 37 openings: the main openings and defences after 1.e4 (Ruy Lopez, Giuoco Piano, Two Knights, Evans Gambit, Scotch, Four Knights, Petrov, Philidor, King's Gambit and King's Gambit Accepted, Vienna, Bishop's Opening, Danish Gambit, Sicilian, French, Caro-Kann, Modern, Alekhine, Scandinavian), after 1.d4 (Queen's Gambit, Accepted and Declined, Slav, Grünfeld, Nimzo-Indian, Queen's Indian, Budapest Gambit, Benko Gambit, Dutch, Trompowsky, Englund Gambit) and 1.c4 (English Opening), and five famous named variations (Berlin Defence and Marshall Attack in the Ruy Lopez, Najdorf and Dragon in the Sicilian, Winawer in the French). Left out because the sources define them differently: the Pirc Defence (lichess and the English Wikipedia: 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6 3.Nc3 g6; the Swedish Wikipedia: 1.e4 d6 2.d4 Nf6), the King's Indian Defence (1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 in the English and Swedish Wikipedia, 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.Nc3 as the shortest lichess line, whose 4.e4 d6 lichess calls the Normal Variation), the Centre Game (2...exd4 or 3.Qxd4; C21 or C22), the Réti Opening (1.Nf3 d5 2.c4, but the name is also used for 1.Nf3), the Smith-Morra Gambit (ECO B20 in the 2002 ECO, B21 in Chess Informant's index, as the English Wikipedia notes). Left out because they are a set-up reached by several move orders: the Catalan Opening (the Swedish Wikipedia: "Dragen kan utföras i olika ordning"), the Semi-Slav Defence, the London System, the King's Indian Attack and the Stonewall. Left out as less common: openings beginning with other first moves (Bird's, Nimzowitsch-Larsen, Sokolsky, Grob and the rest of A00), and minor defences and gambits (Nimzowitsch Defence, Latvian, Elephant and Albin Countergambits, Ponziani, Falkbeer, Old Indian, Bogo-Indian). Named lines inside an opening other than the five variations, traps and transpositions are not covered. The ECO code in each note is the code of the defining line in the 2010 edition of the Encyclopaedia of Chess Openings, as lichess gives it, not the range of the opening family.

"""Fetch the wikitext (with revision ids) of the Swedish and English Wikipedia articles on the candidate openings."""
import json, os, sys, urllib.parse, urllib.request
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
UA = "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)"

def fetch(lang, titles, out):
    result = {}
    for i in range(0, len(titles), 40):
        chunk = titles[i:i + 40]
        url = (f"https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&rvprop=ids|content&rvslots=main"
               f"&format=json&formatversion=2&redirects=1&titles=" + urllib.parse.quote("|".join(chunk)))
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": UA})
        data = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req))
        for p in data["query"]["pages"]:
            if "revisions" in p:
                r = p["revisions"][0]
                result[p["title"]] = {"revid": r["revid"], "text": r["slots"]["main"]["content"]}
            else:
                result[p["title"]] = None
        for r in data["query"].get("redirects", []):
            result.setdefault("_redirects", {})[r["from"]] = r["to"]
    json.dump(result, open(os.path.join(here, out), "w", encoding="utf-8"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
    print(out, len(result))

queries.query:
"""Replay every card's back of authored/chess-openings.json with python-chess.
Checks: move numbers in step; every move legal; every move written exactly as python-chess writes it in SAN
(piece letters, captures, checks, castling O-O); the final position equals the one recorded in the card's
evidence; the back equals the shortest lichess line under the card's lichess name. Mutation test: each back
with its last move replaced by an illegal one must be rejected.
Run from packages/deck-library: uv run --with chess python3 <scratch>/verify_moves.py authored/chess-openings.json"""
import csv, json, os, re, sys
import chess

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DOSSIER = sys.argv[1]  # path of the dossier, e.g. authored/chess-openings.json
sys.path.insert(0, here)
from cards import CARDS
lname = {c[0]: c[1] for c in CARDS}

def replay(moves):
    board = chess.Board()
    for tok in moves.split(" "):
        m = re.match(r"^(\d+)\.(.+)$", tok)
        if m:
            if int(m.group(1)) != board.fullmove_number or board.turn != chess.WHITE:
                raise ValueError(f"move number {tok} out of step")
            tok = m.group(2)
        elif board.turn == chess.WHITE:
            raise ValueError(f"white move {tok} without its number")
        move = board.parse_san(tok)  # raises on illegal or ambiguous
        if board.san(move) != tok:
            raise ValueError(f"{tok} is written {board.san(move)} by python-chess")
        board.push(move)
    return board.fen()

lichess = {}
for f in "abcde":
    with open(os.path.join(here, f"lichess-{f}.tsv"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for r in csv.DictReader(fh, delimiter="\t"):
            pgn = re.sub(r"(\d+)\.\s+", r"\1.", r["pgn"])
            lichess.setdefault(r["name"], []).append(pgn)

d = json.load(open(DOSSIER, encoding="utf-8"))
print("python-chess", chess.__version__)
fails = 0
for c in d["cards"]:
    moves = c["back"]["zxx"]
    try:
        fen = replay(moves)
    except ValueError as e:
        print("FAIL", c["id"], e); fails += 1; continue
    recorded = [e["says"] for e in c["evidence"] if e["source"] == "compilation"][0]
    shortest = min(lichess[lname[c["id"]]], key=lambda p: len(p.split()))
    ok_fen = recorded.endswith(fen)
    ok_lichess = shortest == moves
    # mutation: last move moved to a square no piece of that kind can reach
    toks = moves.split(" ")
    last = toks[-1]
    num = re.match(r"^(\d+\.)?(.*)$", last)
    mutated = " ".join(toks[:-1] + [(num.group(1) or "") + ("Qh8" if num.group(2) != "Qh8" else "Qa1")])
    try:
        replay(mutated); caught = False
    except ValueError:
        caught = True
    status = "ok" if ok_fen and ok_lichess and caught else "FAIL"
    fails += status != "ok"
    print(f"{status} {c['id']}: {moves} | legal | fen {'matches' if ok_fen else 'DIFFERS'} | "
          f"lichess shortest line {'same' if ok_lichess else 'DIFFERS: ' + shortest} | mutation {'caught' if caught else 'MISSED'}")
print(f"{len(d['cards'])} cards, {fails} failures")
